title: Superposition, interference and coherence; Intensity; Reflection and refraction
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: W06-uk1#t3 term and clue written for the game; W04-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; W12-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; W06-uk1#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: W04-1#N.6a, W12-1#N.2, W04-1#N.9a, W12-1#N.13.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Monochromatic
items.clue: Describes light of a single wavelength.

items.label: Wavefront
items.clue: Line or surface joining points that are in phase, such as every crest.

items.label: Point source
items.clue: Small emitter treated as sending its power out equally in all directions.

items.label: Laser
items.clue: Source giving a narrow, intense beam of coherent light; ideal for interference.

questions.stem: The refractive index of a certain plastic is 1.5. Which statement correctly describes what this value means?

options.text: Light travels 1.5 times as fast in the plastic as in a vacuum.
The plastic's density is 1.5 times the density of water.
A ray entering from air is bent to 1/1.5 of its angle of incidence.
Light travels 1.5 times as fast in a vacuum as it does in the plastic.

questions.stem: Sunlight of intensity 1.0 × 10³ W m⁻² falls perpendicularly on a flat solar cell of area 150 cm². At what rate does the sunlight deliver energy to the cell?

A ray of light passes from air into a transparent liquid. The incident ray makes an angle of 40.0° with the surface of the liquid and the refracted ray makes an angle of 55.0° with the surface. The speed of light in air is 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. What is the speed of light in the liquid?
A small source sends out sound equally in all directions. At 2.0 m from the source the intensity is 6.0 × 10⁻³ W m⁻². Ignoring reflections and absorption, what is the intensity 3.0 m from the source?
